newsitem.title: TURKEY: France's de Charette in Turkey for Europe talks.
newsitem.headline: France's de Charette in Turkey for Europe talks.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette met his Turkish counterpart Tansu Ciller on Wednesday at the start of a brief visit expected to focus on Ankara's ties with the European Union.

"France clearly believes that Turkey has potential to take part in the building of Europe," de Charette told reporters at the start of the meeting with Ciller. "We are in agreement with you over the future of Europe."
Turkey's relations with Europe have been strained in recent months by Turkish frustrations at a perceived lack of progress in its bid to become a full member of the European Union.
Ciller reiterated that she wanted Turkey judged on equal terms with other countries, with democracy and human rights being a key criteria.
Turkey's European allies say Ankara's shaky rights record needs to improve before it can be admitted to the union. Ciller says Turkey is taking necessary steps toward improvement.

Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Tuesday strongly criticised the West for the deaths of Turks in a recent spate of fires in Europe, which he said were the result of anti-Moslem sentiment.

"I call to the West, come to your senses. Stop this violence happening among you," Erbakan said in a speech to members of his Islam-based Welfare Party. "You do nothing other than increase tension on earth and apply double standards."
De Charette arrived in Turkey after a visit to feuding neighbours Armenia and Azerbaijan in a bid to help solve the nine-year conflict between them.
He will visit Turkish President Suleyman Demirel later on Wednesday and plans to see other Turkish officials, including Prime Ministe Erbakan, before he leaves on Thursday.
